claims.boundary: The claim is bounded to beating the identity-transition comparator only: on this short-program corpus a simpler memoryless per-step decoder (argmax D·A) outperforms the temporal HMM, so temporal structure shows no net advantage at the authored likelihood and this is recorded explicitly. The identity-transition and temporal decoders share hand-authored A and D (only B differs); a separate supervised held-out fitting path is reported as a distinct generalization diagnostic, and the exit phase is observation-underdetermined.
claims.statement: A left-to-right transition matrix yields a temporal HMM whose forward-filter decoding substantially outperforms the identity-transition comparator on the labelled corpus.

claims.boundary: Controls show the metric is not vacuous; they do not establish external validity beyond the corpus.
claims.statement: Phase-decoding accuracy is discriminative: shuffled-label and uniform-belief negative controls sit near chance, far below the temporal model.

claims.boundary: Segmentation reflects the hand-authored generative model, not a discovered ground-truth control-flow structure.
claims.statement: Smoothed beliefs segment each trace into contiguous program phases that exactly partition the instruction steps.

claims.boundary: Expected free energy genuinely varies across candidates (functional policy, not collapsed), so the corpus tie is a real null — no measurable advantage at this fixture scale — not a non-working policy; the active advantage is shown only as a mechanism in unit tests.
claims.statement: An expected-free-energy active-disassembly policy is implemented; on the short-program corpus it is never worse than a fixed scan and ties because one observation saturates the phase belief.

claims.boundary: The ablation changes only the likelihood conditioning (A) over the same byte corpus; it demonstrates the mechanism behind the head-to-head result, not a claim about real-world binary observation noise. Both directions are measured: no advantage at the authored likelihood, positive advantage at high ambiguity.
claims.statement: The temporal HMM gains a measurable decoding advantage over the memoryless per-step decoder exactly when observations become ambiguous (the authored likelihood is blended toward uniform), and has no net advantage at the authored, near-diagonal likelihood.

claims.boundary: Segmentation reflects the hand-authored generative model, not a discovered ground-truth control-flow structure; the boundary-recovery metric quantifies how well the model's smoothed beliefs align with the authored phase boundaries.
claims.statement: The smoothed forward-backward beliefs segment traces into program phases with a measured, non-trivial boundary F1 and step accuracy against the hand-authored ground truth.

claims.boundary: Calibration is computed from each decoder's own per-step posteriors on the small hand-authored corpus; it reports honest ordering (the temporal model is neither the most accurate nor the best calibrated), not a claim about real-world binary observation noise.
claims.statement: Decoder calibration tracks accuracy on this corpus: the memoryless per-step decoder is the best calibrated (lowest ECE), the temporal model is middle, and the identity-transition comparator is worst.

claims.boundary: Log marginal likelihood is computed from the forward-filter evidence on the small hand-authored corpus; it reports the generative (model-selection) comparison — the temporal model best explains the data even where it is not the best per-step classifier.
claims.statement: The temporal HMM has the highest Bayesian log marginal likelihood of the observed traces (best generative model) even though the memoryless decoder wins on raw per-step accuracy.

claims.boundary: This is supervised estimation on the transparent toy-fixture corpus, not unsupervised phase discovery, population inference, or evidence for general binary-analysis performance.
claims.statement: A smoothed supervised HMM fitting path estimates A, B, and D on training fixtures only and evaluates each excluded fixture in a deterministic leave-one-fixture-out design.

claims.boundary: The semantics are explicitly bounded to the documented immediate-register subset and modeled flag set; unsupported instructions fail closed and this is not a complete x86 lifter, SMT proof, alias analysis, or decompiler.
claims.statement: The implemented transfer-function subset produces an auditable symbolic trace whose pre/post RAX values agree stepwise with independent Unicorn observations, and whose explicitly modeled EFLAGS bits agree on the supported fixtures.

claims.boundary: The check uses the fixed hand-authored A/B/D model and transparent fixture lengths; simulation intervals are descriptive model-checking intervals, not posterior uncertainty, population inference, or evidence that the model has discovered phases.
claims.statement: A fixed-parameter HMM generative adequacy check compares observed fixture phase structure with same-length simulations and reports which observed metrics fall inside central simulation intervals.

claims.boundary: The typed and factorized layers are a supervised, fixture-level companion to the collapsed categorical HMM; they do not establish independent semantic discovery, conditional independence of fields, external validity, or improved performance on arbitrary binaries.
claims.statement: A label-blind typed observation schema retains static Capstone fields and bounded dynamic status, and its factorized and hierarchical companion scores are evaluated with fixture-level holdouts, field-family ablations, and an explicit missing-field policy.

claims.boundary: Coverage is a design diagnostic over hand-authored toy fixtures; it is not independent binary sampling, external validity, or evidence that any typed field is intrinsic program semantics.
claims.statement: The expanded transparent fixture corpus contains source-bound variation in bounded memory operands, repeated authored phases, and static-versus-dynamic branch paths, and the coverage inventory records that variation before any richer model is promoted.

claims.boundary: The experiment uses equal normalized proxy costs and transparent toy fixtures; it is a sensor-choice mechanism test, not evidence of autonomous sensing, real execution cost, or general reverse-engineering performance.
claims.statement: A bounded action-conditioned policy can choose typed field queries from training-only predictive likelihoods before revealing held-out values, and its acquisition budget can be compared with fixed, seeded-random, and explicitly inadmissible oracle policies.

claims.boundary: The estimator uses an ordered-state scaffold, a reference-model initialization, a positive transition-support prior, and the authored transparent toy fixture corpus; its held-out accuracy is a finite implementation diagnostic, not evidence of unsupervised semantic discovery, identifiable phase meanings, or general binary-analysis performance.
claims.statement: An ordered categorical HMM can be fit by observation-only Baum-Welch expectation-maximization on training-fixture observation IDs, with phase labels reserved for held-out scoring and a complete-fixture comparison against supervised MAP and the fixed reference model.

claims.boundary: A roadmap receipt is a design and integrity contract, not evidence that the planned identifiability, theorem, external-validity, or replication milestones have been achieved.

limitations: This is a source-bound generated artifact. Its domain-specific validator defines the evidence boundary; the receipt alone is not a scientific claim.
